papers.authors: Li T, Zou T, Li Z, Liu Z, Chen J, Xiong Y, Li M, Zhang X et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Digital Medicine, College of Biomedical Engineering and Medical Imaging, Army Medical University (Third Mi…

papers.abstract_en: Immunochemotherapy (ICT) is a critical treatment for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC), yet predicting individual response remains challenging. We developed a three-channel 3D deep learning framework integrating tumor habitat analysis for predicting ICT response. In this multicenter retrospective study of 277 patients, voxel-level clustering of pretreatment CT images segmented tumors into habitat subregions reflecting microenvironmental heterogeneity. A ResNet-50 model incorporating habitat maps, cropped tumor images, and ROI masks achieved an AUC of 0.927 (95% CI, 0.850-0.951) in the independent external test cohort, compared with 0.869 for habitat radiomics (DeLong p = 0.343). SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified texture features, particularly gray-level co-occurrence matrix correlation in habitat 3, as the primary contributors. This framework provides a noninvasive approach for predicting ICT response in LA-ESCC.

papers.title_zh: EGFR突变晚期NSCLC一线奥希替尼的基线临床与分子预后因素：系统评价与荟萃分析（TP53突变、EGFR L858R、ECOG PS≥2与脑转移与更差生存相关）
papers.title_en: Clinical and molecular prognostic factors associated with outcomes of first-line osimertinib in EGFR-Mutated advanced NSCLC: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Ruan Y, Xue H, Long C, Cao W, Han J, Zhang T
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, The First People's Hospital of Jiande, Jiande, China.
papers.results: TP53突变与更短PFS/rwPFS相关（HR 1.65, 95%CI 1.15-2.37），并与更差OS/rwOS相关（HR 1.55, 95%CI 1.14-2.12）；EGFR L858R对比19外显子缺失与更短PFS/rwPFS相关（HR 1.62, 95%CI 1.39-1.90）及更差OS/rwOS（HR 1.63, 95%CI 1.40-1.88），敏感性分析结果一致；ECOG PS≥2、中枢神经系统/脑转移、肝转移与更差结局相关；肝转移与OS/rwOS的关联对替代效应量选择敏感；骨转移与PD-L1表达的证据稳健性较差。
papers.authors_conclusion: 证据分级评定将EGFR L858R、ECOG PS≥2和中枢神经系统/脑转移列为高确定性不良预后因素；肝转移对PFS/rwPFS为中等确定性，对OS/rwOS确定性较低；TP53突变、PD-L1表达和骨转移为较低确定性或探索性发现。这些结果支持未来构建整合预后模型，但不足以确立在一线奥希替尼单药之上选择强化治疗的标准。
papers.ai_note: 检索截止日期写作2026年5月20日，晚于常规可核实时点，需核对；摘要仅给出TP53与L858R的合并HR，ECOG PS≥2、脑转移、肝转移、骨转移、PD-L1均无任何数值，却据此作出“高/中/低确定性”分级，分级依据（GRADE域、偏倚风险、异质性I²、发表偏倚）未报告；纳入研究多为真实世界回顾性队列，混杂调整不一致，预后因素合并结果易受未调整混杂影响；“高确定性”表述与二手数据证据强度不相称；主要终点PFS/rwPFS与OS/rwOS混并（临床研究PFS与真实世界rwPFS合并），削弱可解释性。

pico.p: 18项研究、4,070例接受一线奥希替尼治疗的EGFR突变晚期/复发/转移性NSCLC患者
pico.ic: 暴露/预后因素（TP53突变、EGFR L858R对比19外显子缺失、ECOG PS≥2、中枢神经系统/脑转移、肝转移、骨转移、PD-L1表达）与结局（PFS/rwPFS为主要结局，OS/rwOS为次要结局）的关联；无干预对照

papers.reason: 为EGFR突变晚期NSCLC一线奥希替尼的患者风险分层提供合并效应量基线，可用于预后模型构建与强化治疗试验的富集人群设计（如TP53突变、L858R、脑转移亚组），但不足以单独改变一线用药选择。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is the standard first-line therapy for epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but outcomes remain heterogeneous. This meta-analysis evaluated baseline clinical and molecular prognostic factors associated with poorer outcomes in this setting. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 20 May 2026. Eligible studies included patients with EGFR-mutated advanced, recurrent, or metastatic NSCLC receiving first-line osimertinib with extractable prognostic data. The primary outcome was progression-free survival or real-world progression-free survival (PFS/rwPFS); overall survival or real-world overall survival (OS/rwOS) was secondary. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models. RESULTS: Eighteen studies involving 4,070 first-line osimertinib-treated patients were included. TP53 mutation was associated with shorter PFS/rwPFS (HR 1.65, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-2.37) and worse OS/rwOS (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.14-2.12). EGFR L858R, versus exon 19 deletion, was associated with shorter PFS/rwPFS (HR 1.62, 95% CI 1.39-1.90) and worse OS/rwOS (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.40-1.88), with consistent estimates across sensitivity analyses. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status ≥ 2, central nervous system/brain metastasis, and liver metastasis were associated with poorer outcomes. The OS/rwOS association for liver metastasis was sensitive to alternative estimate selection. Evidence for bone metastasis and programmed death-ligand 1 expression was less robust. CONCLUSIONS: Evidence-tier assessment identified EGFR L858R, ECOG PS ≥ 2, and CNS/brain metastasis as high-certainty adverse prognostic factors. Liver metastasis was supported by moderate certainty for PFS/rwPFS but lower certainty for OS/rwOS. TP53 mutation, PD-L1 expression, and bone metastasis were lower-certainty or exploratory findings. These findings support future integrated prognostic models, but do not establish criteria for selecting intensified first-line therapy over osimertinib monotherapy.

papers.title_zh: 规划器-执行器式多模态智能体系统回答肺癌筛查CT患者提问：模拟问题上的工具调用准确率与“转诊医生”自我调节能力评估
papers.title_en: Planner-Executor Style Multimodal Agentic System to Answer Patient Questions in Lung Cancer Screening CT.
papers.authors: Sakiyama K, Serapio A, Ye M, Nowroozi A, Bondarenko M, Wu YF, Qi K, Liu J et al.
papers.authors_conclusion: 规划器-执行器式多模态智能体系统能可靠回答LCS相关的患者个体化问题；其较高的工具调用与自我调节表现显示其有潜力成为LCS项目中安全有效的数字化沟通辅助工具。
papers.ai_note: ①问题为模拟生成而非真实患者提问，未验证真实语境下的提问分布与误解模式；②“自我调节准确率”以LLM-as-a-judge判定，缺少医师金标准对照，属循环式评价风险；③工具调用分母694与699题不一致，5题缺失原因未说明；④“100条回答×4名医师”与结果中228/172的分母关系需读者自行推断，报告口径不清；⑤仅报告“全 reader 满分5.0”这一严苛但粗糙的比例，未给均值/分布或失败案例的错误类型分析；⑥无与基线模型、检索式问答或人工护士/医师回答的对照；⑦单中心回顾性数据，无真实随访依从性等临床结局。

pico.p: 某三级学术医院116份肺癌筛查（LCS）CT报告及图像；基于此生成699个模拟患者问题（分为可回答与应转诊医生两类）；医师阅片评分子集为4名医师×100条回答
pico.ic: 干预：基于大语言模型的多智能体（planner+executor）多模态智能体系统，用于回答LCS CT结果相关问题；对照：无对照组，仅以工具调用准确率、自我调节准确率（LLM-as-a-judge）及医师评分（临床准确性、患者可理解性）为评价指标

papers.reason: 为肺癌筛查结果沟通类AI工具提供了可复用的评价框架（工具调用、越界问题转诊、医师多维评分），可作为后续真实患者场景研究与数字沟通工具对照设计的基线；但尚不足以改变当前筛查随访或患者沟通的临床路径。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Accurate patient understanding of lung cancer screening (LCS) results is critical for engagement and follow-up adherence, given the currently low screening uptake. While artificial intelligence (AI) systems show promise in facilitating patient communication, its effective use in clinical settings requires appropriate invocation of imaging tools and self-regulation by deferring certain questions to physicians. To this end, we developed and evaluated a planner-executor style multimodal agentic system to answer simulated patient questions about LCS CT results. METHODS: This retrospective study utilized 116 LCS CT reports and images collected from a tertiary academic hospital. The system employed a multi-agent architecture (planner and executor) to mimic clinical reasoning. We developed a large language model (LLM)-based question generation framework to prepare a comprehensive set of 699 simulated patient questions, categorized as answerable and defer-to-doctor to assess self-regulation. Performance was evaluated on tool-calling, self-regulation accuracy (ability to correctly defer out-of-scope questions to a human provider) assessed by LLM-as-a-judge, and clinical quality assessed by a reader performance study with four physicians evaluating a subset of 100 responses. RESULTS: The system demonstrated high overall tool-calling accuracy of 93.1% (646/694; 95% CI: 91.2%, 95.0%) and self-regulation accuracy of 92.6% (462/499; 90.2%, 94.8%). For answerable questions, the percentage of responses receiving perfect 5.0 scores across all readers included 78.9% (180/228) for clinical accuracy (inter-rater agreement: Gwet's AC2=0.92), and 73.2% (167/228) for patient understandability (0.86). For defer-to-doctor questions, the percentage of responses included 77.3% (133/172) for clinical accuracy (0.80) and 70.3% (121/172) for patient understandability (0.78). CONCLUSIONS: The planner-executor style multi-modal agentic system reliably answers patient-specific questions about LCS. Its high tool-calling and self-regulation performance demonstrates its potential as a safe and effective digital communication facilitator in LCS programs.

papers.title_en: Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery versus Thoracotomy in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Survival Analysis and Exploratory Predictive Modelling.
papers.authors: Makarov V, Baimukhametov E, Yessentayeva S, Oljaev S, Arybzhanov D
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Multidisciplinary Surgery, National Research Oncology Centre, Astana, Republic of Kazakhstan.
papers.results: VATS术后死亡率0%（0% versus 5.8% for thoracotomy）；I期中位总生存65.3 versus 67.7个月（p=0.768）；II期75.8 versus 48.8个月（p=0.003）；III期方向相似但未达统计学显著（摘要未给出数值）；探索性模型测试准确度0.39–0.48。
papers.authors_conclusion: In this unadjusted retrospective cohort, VATS was associated with lower perioperative mortality, and at stage II with longer overall survival. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: This study retrospectively compared outcomes of minimally invasive and open surgical approaches for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a cohort of 255 patients operated on between 2014 and 2018. A machine-learning analysis was performed as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating component. METHOD: Survival was analysed by disease stage using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests. Because the groups were not randomised and were imbalanced at baseline, comparisons are unadjusted and should be interpreted as associations. Exploratory predictive models were developed using five machine-learning algorithms (random forest performing best), with feature contributions interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP). Missing values were handled by multiple imputation, continuous variables were standardised, and correlated features were excluded. RESULTS: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) was used more frequently for adenocarcinoma, in women, and at stage I, with zero postoperative mortality (0% versus 5.8% for thoracotomy). At stage I, there were no differences in median overall survival (65.3 versus 67.7 months; p=0.768); at stage II, VATS was associated with longer survival (75.8 versus 48.8 months; p=0.003); at stage III, a similar direction did not reach significance. Recurrent predictors in the exploratory models were coronary artery disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, intervention volume, tumour histology, and vascular invasion; however, test accuracy remained low (0.39-0.48), precluding clinical use. SHAP analysis highlighted resection completeness, lack of conversion, and tumour morphology. CONCLUSIONS: In this unadjusted retrospective cohort, VATS was associated with lower perioperative mortality, and at stage II with longer overall survival. Given the retrospective design and baseline imbalances, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective, adjusted studies before informing surgical indications.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: For patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for lung cancer or other pulmonary lesions, effective one-lung ventilation (OLV) is essential to provide surgical exposure. Bronchial blockers (BBs) are increasingly used for OLV, but the optimal management of their vent port to accelerate lung collapse remains unclear. METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, controlled trial, 75 patients were allocated to three groups (n = 25 each): Group 1-BB with vent port closed; Group 2 (control)-BB with vent port open; Group 3-BB with the disconnection technique. Primary outcome was the time to complete lung collapse, which was scored according to the video clips obtained during the operation. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hypoxemia, blood gas analysis, blocker malposition, perioperative complications, and surgeon satisfaction. RESULTS: A total of 72 patients were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis, with 24 patients in each group. Median time to complete lung collapse was 15 min (95% CI: 10-15) in Groups 1 and 3 but was not reached in Group 2 (15/24, 62.5% had not achieved complete collapse by 30 min). In an exploratory 30-min restricted mean survival time (RMST), complete collapse occurred on average 14.17 min earlier in Group 1 (95% CI: 11.10-17.23) and 12.50 min earlier in Group 3 (95% CI: 9.62-15.38) than in Group 2, with no difference between Groups 1 and 3 (1.67 min, 95% CI: -1.85 to 5.19); time-averaged hazard ratios were consistent (Group 1 vs. 2, 9.80 [4.22-22.73]; Group 3 vs. 2, 7.63 [3.36-17.31]; Group 1 vs. 3, 1.20 [0.67-2.16]). No significant differences were detected in hypoxemia, blocker malposition, or complications across groups; however, the trial was not powered for safety outcomes. CONCLUSION: In patients aged 18-65 years with ASA I-II and normal pulmonary function undergoing thoracic surgery, the closure of the BB vent port results in a more rapid lung collapse compared to maintaining the vent port open. However, there was no statistically significant difference observed between the vent port closure technique and the disconnection technique regarding the time required for complete lung collapse. papers.abstract_en: Two randomized trials, CALGB 140503 and JCOG0802, established segmentectomy as an oncologically acceptable alternative to lobectomy for small, peripheral, clinically node-negative non-small cell lung cancer. Both reached that conclusion under a protocol-enforced condition that is rarely emphasized when their results are applied in practice: nodal status had to be verified intraoperatively against a defined anatomic standard. CALGB 140503 required frozen-section confirmation of N0 status at two mediastinal stations and one major hilar node before randomization, whereas JCOG0802 mandated systematic or selective dissection of N1 and N2 stations in both arms and explicitly disallowed sampling as a substitute. This review examines whether that nodal rigor is reproduced, or even reported, once segmentectomy leaves the trial setting. National data indicate that it is not. Segmentectomy accounts for 4.4% of resections for clinical stage I to IIA disease, and only 12.6% of segmentectomy cases met all three Commission on Cancer quality measures, with adherence concentrated in academic and higher-volume programs. Retrospective series consistently report lower nodal upstaging after segmentectomy than after lobectomy, but the difference is driven by N1 rather than N2 stations and tracks the smaller nodal footprint of the operation, so a lower upstaging rate cannot by itself distinguish less disease from less looking. Anatomic mapping data indicate that exhaustive intersegmental dissection is unnecessary, whereas reliable hilar and mediastinal sampling is not. Across the wider literature, adequate nodal evaluation is defined inconsistently and reported at a granularity too coarse for readers to verify compliance, a two-axis problem that we characterize here for the segmentectomy literature specifically. Robotic assistance increases the number of nodal stations harvested relative to video-assisted surgery but has not been shown to improve risk-adjusted detection of occult disease. We propose a seven-point minimum standard, anchored on station-based rather than count-based adequacy, for segmentectomy performed outside a clinical trial.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) features a poor prognosis and unclear pathogenesis, and the role of R-loops, key regulators of genome stability, has not been systematically characterized in this disease. METHODS: Transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing data of ESCC were integrated with published R-loop-related genes (RLRGs) to construct an RLRG scoring system. The associations between the RLRG score and prognosis, tumor immune microenvironment, and tumor stemness were analyzed via multiple bioinformatics algorithms. The expression of core genes was verified using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Western Blot, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence. RESULTS: Seven key RLRGs related to the prognosis of the ESCC patients were identified, among which three core genes-BRIX1, CHEK1, and NUP155-were significantly upregulated in ESCC tissues compared with controls, as confirmed by both bioinformatic analysis and experimental validation. Notably, BRIX1, CHEK1, and NUP155 were co-enriched in DNA replication, pyrimidine metabolism, RNA degradation, and MYC target pathways, which are closely linked to R-loop biology and suggest potential crosstalk between these genes and R-loop regulatory networks. Meanwhile, the low RLRGs score group exhibited significantly worse overall survival but displayed a more active yet dysfunctional immune microenvironment. Single-cell analysis identified SquamousEpithelium cells as the key cell type with the highest RLRG scores across five independent algorithms. Malignant SquamousEpithelium cells with high RLRG scores showed enhanced stemness and activation of pathways including JAK-STAT, hypoxia, and DNA repair. CONCLUSION: This study provided the first systematic characterization of the R-loop landscape in ESCC, suggests that SquamousEpithelium cells may play a key role in R-loop-associated progression and are identified as potential prognostic biomarkers with possible therapeutic relevance that requires functional validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Smoking is the primary cause of lung cancer, the leading cause of cancer-related mortality in Norway. To inform disease modeling and tobacco control policies, including lung cancer screening, we estimated sex-specific, birth-cohort smoking behaviors among Norwegians born between 1950 and 2000 using national survey data. METHODS: We analyzed nationally representative cross-sectional survey data from 1978 to 2024 (n = 78,282) to reconstruct smoking trends and smoking intensity in Norway. We used a previously established Age-Period-Cohort modeling framework to estimate cohort-specific prevalence of daily ever-smoking, probabilities of smoking initiation and cessation, prevalence of daily current-smoking, and average cigarettes smoked per day (CPD). Analyses were conducted separately by sex assigned at birth for cohorts born between 1950 and 2000. FINDINGS: Daily ever-smoking prevalence peaked in the 1950 birth cohort, reaching 70% (90% CI 66%-91%) among males and 66% (90% CI 55%-89%) among females, alongside similar peaks in smoking initiation probabilities, 13% (90% CI 12%-24%) for males and 12% (90% CI 10%-23%) for females. Smoking cessation probabilities increased with age within each birth cohort, rising from approximately 0% to 5% over 40 years in earlier cohorts, compared with an increase from about 5% to 15% over 20 years from the 1965 birth cohort onward. Smoking intensity peaked at 15 CPD among males and 12 CPD among females. Although smoking intensity declined in both sexes after the 1975 birth cohort, it remained higher among males, with peak model-estimated CPD decreasing from approximately 13.5 to 10 cigarettes in males and from 11.5 to 7.5 cigarettes in females between the 1980 and 2000 birth cohorts. INTERPRETATION: Smoking behavior in Norway has changed across generations, with declining smoking initiation rates, increased smoking cessation, and lower cigarettes per day. Understanding these trends provides essential inputs to inform tobacco control and lung cancer prevention policies in Norway. For CCA, OS and PFS were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves and used directly, with a base-case ICER and extrapolation sensitivity. The wholesale acquisition cost was $24,155.46/infusion. Probabilistic, one-way, and threshold analyses were performed.ResultsFor NSCLC and PDAC, ICERs ranged from approximately $665,000 (PDAC, OS 18 months) to $2.79 million per QALY (NSCLC, OS 10 months). Cost-effectiveness required acquisition-cost reductions of 60% to 91%.ConclusionsAt its current price, zenocutuzumab is not cost-effective for any approved indication, whether OS is unobserved (NSCLC, PDAC) or observed (CCA). papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is highly heterogeneous, leading to limited drug effectiveness and resistance. Antibody therapies offer limited benefits due to low response rates. Multispecific antibodies, targeting multiple tumor antigens and natural killer (NK)-cell receptors, may overcome these challenges, but their effectiveness in ESCC therapy is not yet understood. METHODS: Transcriptome sequencing and database analysis were performed on samples from patients with ESCC to identify tumor antigens. Multispecific antibodies were designed to target tumor antigens and NK-cell surface markers. Fast protein liquid chromatography and surface plasmon resonance were applied for quality control of antibodies. Using multiple ESCC cell lines and NK cells from different donors, flow cytometry was performed to assess NK cell cytotoxicity and activation. Immunofluorescence assays were used to confirm colocalization. Transcriptome sequencing, flow cytometry and western blots were performed to explore molecular mechanisms. Subcutaneous and metastatic xenograft tumor models were established to evaluate the in vivo antitumor efficacy of antibodies combined with adoptive transfer of NK cells. RESULTS: The expression of EGFR was consistently highly expressed in all ESCC samples, while MET was specifically upregulated in recurrent ESCC, whereas the database also validated two antigens overexpression in tumor tissues. Antibodies were successfully engineered for multiple antigens binding. The tetraspecific antibodies significantly enhanced NK-cell cytotoxicity by up to 30% against ESCC and paclitaxel-resistant cell lines compared with the NK-only group in vitro. Transcriptomic analysis and experimental validation revealed that antibodies triggered immune activation pathways and increased the expression of tumor necrosis factor-α, interferon-γ, and granzyme B in NK cells, but also induced NK cell exhaustion. In vivo, tetraspecific antibodies combined with NK cell infusions exerted superior antitumor efficacy, with an 82.3% tumor volume reduction in the early-stage model and 65.7% in the advanced-stage model compared with controls. The therapeutic efficacy was also observed in the metastatic tumor model. Meanwhile, the combination therapy was well tolerated, with enhanced NK cell infiltration in tumor tissues. CONCLUSIONS: We developed tetraspecific antibodies to effectively bridge ESCC cells and NK cells. The antibodies have the potential to enhance the antitumor activity of NK cells against ESCC. This study supports the clinical translation of tetraspecific antibodies for NK cell-based immunotherapy for ESCC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) has greatly expanded the identification of rare germline variants in hereditary cancer predisposition. However, the interpretation of variants of uncertain significance (VUS), particularly in novel candidate genes, remains a major challenge in lung cancer genetics. OBJECTIVE: To functionally characterize selected germline variants identified by WES in patients with familial or suspected hereditary lung cancer and provide evidence for their prioritization. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Three splicing variants in HGS, CDK12, and CEACAM5 genes were investigated by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing to assess their effect on splicing. Candidate missense variants were analyzed through protein-protein interaction network analysis, gene expression profiling, and structure-based computational modeling to evaluate their potential impact on protein stability and molecular interactions. RESULTS: RNA analysis confirmed that the CDK12 variant produced the previously reported in-frame one amino acid deletion, whereas the HGS variant activated a cryptic splice acceptor site, resulting in an in-frame deletion affecting a region containing a known ubiquitination site. No aberrant splicing was detected for CEACAM5. Network analyses highlighted convergence of three candidate genes (ERBB3, MAP2K1 and RASA2) on receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and the RAS/MAPK pathway. Structural analyses predicted local perturbations affecting membrane interactions, residue interaction networks, or protein stability for variants in the three previous genes and in USP4, supporting their functional relevance. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating RNA-based functional assays with network and structural analyses provides a practical framework for interpreting and prioritizing rare germline VUS identified by WES, supporting the identification of candidate lung cancer susceptibility genes and improving genetic risk assessment.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Functional assays can assist individualised selection of treatment regimens by evaluating the ex vivo response of tumour cells to anticancer therapeutics. However, the two major strategies used to assess responses to targeted drugs, target-based profiling and phenotypic profiling, have inherent limitations. Target-based profiling does not directly capture downstream cell-fate outcomes, whereas phenotypic profiling provides limited mechanistic information on drug action. METHODS: Live-cell fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) microscopy was used to integrate the interaction between EGFRL858R and GRB2 with cellular phenotypic features, thereby predicting the efficacy of EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) at the single-cell level. RESULTS: The target-based drug score (T-score), derived from the interaction between EGFRL858R and GRB2 in living cells co-expressing CFP-EGFRL858R and YFP-GRB2, enabled evaluation of the on-target activity of EGFR-TKIs against EGFRL858R. The phenotype drug score (P-score), constructed from cellular phenotype features, characterised the phenotypic responses induced by EGFR-TKIs. The TP-score, integrating the T- and P-scores, accurately predicted the efficacy of EGFR-TKIs. In living H3255 cells, the TP-score of osimertinib (OSI) was higher than that of gefitinib (GEF). Notably, in H3255 cell-derived xenograft (CDX) mouse models, OSI showed superior in vivo antitumour efficacy compared with GEF. Furthermore, live-cell TP scoring revealed that primary tumour cells from a patient with NSCLC did not respond to OSI, a finding consistent with the absence of actionable EGFR mutations in this patient. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the clinical feasibility of predicting EGFR-TKI efficacy by integrating EGFRL858R-GRB2 interactions with cellular phenotypic features in single living cells.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary resection is a primary treatment for patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer, but removal of lung tissue can result in significant changes in postoperative pulmonary function and patient recovery. This review examines changes in pulmonary function tests (PFTs) and patient-reported outcomes following lung resection, with consideration of differences among surgical procedures and postoperative timepoints. Across studies, pulmonary function demonstrated its greatest decline during the early postoperative period, followed by gradual improvement during subsequent follow-up. However, pulmonary function generally remained below preoperative values, with the magnitude of decline influenced by the extent of lung tissue removed. Patients undergoing lobectomy or pneumonectomy generally experienced greater postoperative reductions than those undergoing sublobar procedures, although outcomes also varied according to the lobe and number of segments resected. Patient-reported outcomes, including dyspnea, pain, physical function, and quality of life, similarly worsened during early recovery but generally improved over time, with some measures returning to baseline. Preoperative pulmonary function, particularly DLCO, remains important for assessing a patient's ability to tolerate resection, while postoperative oxygen requirements are influenced by pulmonary function, patient characteristics, and postoperative complications. Additionally, decreased physical activity after surgery was associated with non-recovery of DLCO. Overall, postoperative pulmonary function follows a pattern of early decline followed by gradual recovery, although complete return to baseline is uncommon. These findings emphasize the importance of evaluating both pulmonary function and patient-reported outcomes when considering the consequences of pulmonary resection.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has become a biomarker-driven disease, yet durable control remains limited by therapeutic resistance, metabolic heterogeneity, and incomplete predictors of response. Cuproptosis, a copper-dependent form of regulated cell death linked to mitochondrial respiration and lipoylated TCA-cycle proteins, offers a potential metabolic layer for patient stratification. However, the current NSCLC literature is dominated by cuproptosis-related gene scores, lncRNA models, and immune-association signatures. These studies are useful for hypothesis generation but rarely demonstrate copper flux, FDX1 dependence, lipoylated DLAT/DLST engagement, iron-sulfur cluster protein loss, or pathway-specific pharmacodynamics. We therefore organize the NSCLC literature using a mechanistic evidence matrix that separates transcriptomic association, copper-access enrichment, mitochondrial-dependence evidence, canonical target engagement, and clinical pharmacodynamic confirmation. Rather than proposing a new molecular subtype or diagnostic label, we conceptualize cuproptosis susceptibility as a continuous, mechanism-based construct defined by copper access, TCA/OXPHOS dependence, lipoylated substrate burden, detoxification capacity, and immune context. This framework reframes cuproptosis from universal copper toxicity to a conditional therapeutic vulnerability. Its clinical value will depend on biomarker-enriched trials with pharmacodynamic confirmation rather than retrospective gene signatures alone.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) shows marked heterogeneity in its immune microenvironment, which may contribute to differences in disease-free survival (DFS) and clinical outcome. Although current LUAD classifications are largely based on genomic or transcriptomic features, immune subtypes defined directly from bulk proteomic data remain poorly characterized. Here, we used an immune-cell proteomic reference matrix to investigate proteome-defined immune states in LUAD and to identify prognostically relevant immune subtypes. METHODS: A quantitative human immune-cell proteomic reference matrix was integrated with LUAD tumor proteomic profiles. The reference matrix covered seven major immune lineages and 26 immune-cell states. The discovery cohort included 101 LUAD tumor proteomes with matched clinical information. After gene symbol matching and normalization, proteome-defined immune-cell state signals were estimated for each sample using non-negative constrained regression. These signals were then used for unsupervised subtype identification and DFS analysis. An independent Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC)-LUAD cohort was used for validation, with subtype analysis performed at the immune-cell marker protein module level. RESULTS: The immune-cell reference matrix contained 8400 quantified proteins, and 2381 proteins were retained for modeling. Based on 26 proteome-defined immune-cell state signals, LUAD samples separated into two immune proteomic subtypes. In the discovery cohort, Subtype 2 had significantly worse DFS than Subtype 1 (log-rank p = 0.0047; HR = 2.09, 95% CI 1.24-3.54). In the Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC)-LUAD validation cohort, marker protein module-based analysis again identified two subtypes with distinct DFS outcomes. The high-risk Subtype 2 showed higher Granulocyte and Myeloid/DC modules, whereas the low-risk Subtype 1 showed higher B cell, T cell, and NK-cell modules. Subtype 2 was associated with shorter DFS in the validation cohort (log-rank p = 0.0061; HR = 3.45, 95% CI: 1.35-8.82), and this association remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, and stage. CONCLUSIONS: Proteomic immune profiling identified two prognostically distinct immune subtypes in LUAD. The poor-DFS subtype was characterized by increased myeloid/granulocyte-related protein modules, whereas the favorable-DFS subtype showed stronger B cell-, T cell-, and NK cell-related signals. These findings support the use of bulk tumor proteomics to characterize clinically relevant immune heterogeneity in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer screening (LCS) remains underutilized, with 18% uptake nationally, despite established evidence-based guidelines, particularly among women who engage with preventive care through breast cancer screening (BCS). We characterized baseline LCS uptake and its correlates among women receiving BCS at two participating hospitals. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using six years of electronic health record data (October 2019-November 2025) from Barnes-Jewish West County Hospital and Christian Hospital. Women aged 50-80 with any documented smoking history were included. The primary outcome was LCS uptake, defined as evidence of at least one low-dose computed tomography scan. We conducted multivariable logistic regression models and assessed for effect modification by race and area deprivation using likelihood ratio tests. Results Of 9,686 women with smoking history, 3,209 (33.1%) had received at least one LCS. Pack-year documentation status (AOR 2.90; 95% CI: 2.63, 3.19), tobacco cessation medication use (AOR 2.21; 95% CI: 1.98, 2.48), and current smoking (AOR 1.84; 95% CI: 1.64, 2.07) were the factors most strongly associated with uptake. Alcohol use was associated with lower odds of LCS uptake (0.81, 95% CI: 0.73, 0.89). Effect modification by race and area deprivation were not significant. Conclusions Baseline LCS uptake exceeded the national average; however, racial disparities were observed. Completeness of smoking history documentation, tobacco cessation medication use, and current smoking status were strongly associated with LCS uptake. These findings highlight the need for strategies to improve smoking history documentation and promote tobacco cessation efforts in cancer screening programs and establish the baseline against which the Pink & Pearl program, a co-located breast and lung cancer screening initiative at these sites, will be evaluated.

CONCLUSIONS: The revised ypT/ypN-based stage grouping improved prognostic ordering and model fit in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, while maintaining comparable discrimination. This approach may support postoperative risk stratification after neoadjuvant therapy and esophagectomy.

papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: In advanced stages, lung adenocarcinoma obstructs airways and disrupts ventilation-perfusion relationships in the lung, causing systemic hypoxemia and enabling a feed-forward loop that accelerates malignancy. Systemic hypoxemia is also experienced due to common respiratory comorbidities such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), potentially accelerating malignancy. In a statewide electronic health record network, pre-existing COPD (598 matched pairs) or sleep apnea (235 matched pairs) independently predicted worse survival following incident lung cancer diagnosis. Since the mechanistic basis of the link between malignancy and hypoxia is not well understood, we created systemic hypoxia in Kras LSL- G12D/+ ;Trp53 fl/fl (KP) mice by delivering low inspired oxygen concentrations (8% inspired oxygen; 8 h daily). Hypoxia nearly doubled tumor multiplicity and selectively remodeled cancer central carbon metabolism. Spatially resolved metabolomics revealed marked tumor-compartment glycogen accumulation, elevated tricarboxylic-acid cycle intermediates, and depleted glycolytic pools. Quantitative proteomics across cellular models and autochthonous tumors demonstrated that systemic hypoxia drives glycogen mobilization selectively through the lysosomal enzyme acid α-glucosidase (GAA). Tumor-cell-autonomous deletion of GAA eliminated the hypoxia-driven growth advantage and disrupted downstream anabolic biosynthetic pathways. Thus, systemic hypoxia drives lung adenocarcinoma expansion by mobilizing lysosomal glycogen reserves through GAA to sustain proliferative growth. ETOC BLURB: Lung tumors compromise pulmonary gas exchange, driving systemic hypoxemia that accelerates malignancy. Comorbidities such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and obstructive sleep apnea compound this hypoxemic burden. Clarke et al. isolate systemic hypoxia in mice, showing it doubles lung tumor multiplicity by inducing glycogen degradation through lysosomal acid α-glucosidase (GAA). Deleting GAA eliminates this hypoxic growth advantage.

In stage IV disease, the absolute change in 1-year survival was largest in the 'no treatment' group (24.44%) and in 2-year survival in the 'surgery ± additional treatment' group (33.46%). papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) mediastinal mass excision has become the standard approach for anterior mediastinal lesions. Understanding its learning curve is essential for surgical training and quality assurance. The primary objective was to quantify the association between cumulative case experience (case sequence number) and operative time, the primary outcome, using cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis and multivariable regression modelling. We tested the null hypothesis that operative time does not change with increasing case sequence after adjustment for patient-, tumour- and country-related factors. Secondary objectives were to estimate the number of cases required to achieve proficiency and to compare perioperative outcomes across learning phases and between participating countries. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted at five academic and tertiary-care centers in Egypt and Saudi Arabia between January 2023 and December 2025. Seventy-seven consecutive patients undergoing VATS excision of mediastinal masses were categorized into three phases: Early (first 20 cases), Intermediate (next 20 cases), and Late (last 37 cases). Cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis was performed. Operative outcomes, including operative time, blood loss, conversion rate, and postoperative complications, were compared across phases and between countries (Egypt vs. Saudi Arabia). Multivariable linear regression and a linear mixed-effects model with participating centre as a random intercept were used to identify factors independently associated with operative time. papers.abstract_en: Background The management of suspected malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is often variable, with many patients undergoing repeated pleural aspirations before a definitive management decision is made. The RED (respiratory rate, effusion depth and dyspnoea) score is a recently derived and validated tool that predicts the time to the next pleural fluid drainage procedure. We describe a single-center, before-and-after quality improvement project (QIP) evaluating the introduction of a structured proforma incorporating clinical pre-test probability and the RED score into routine pleural clinic assessment. Methods A retrospective baseline cycle (Cycle 1, n=48) was compared with a prospective intervention cycle (Cycle 2, n=26) following the implementation of a structured assessment pro forma. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients experiencing unplanned emergency admission or earlier-than-planned pleural clinic review within three months of the index pleural procedure. Secondary outcomes included the proportion of patients requiring more than two pleural procedures and the proportion of patients achieving definitive pleural management within three months. Categorical variables were compared using Fisher's exact test given the small sample sizes; results are presented with risk differences, 95% confidence intervals, and odds ratios where calculable. No a priori power calculation was performed, and this exploratory before-and-after design does not permit causal inferences. Results In Cycle 1, 16/48 patients (33.3%) experienced an emergency admission or unplanned pleural clinic review, compared with 2/26 (7.7%) in Cycle 2 (Fisher's exact test, P=0.021; risk difference -25.6%, 95% CI -42.5 to -8.8; odds ratio 6.0). The proportion of patients requiring more than two pleural procedures fell from 33.3% to 22.7% (P=0.415, not statistically significant). Cytology was positive in 24/48 (50.0%) Cycle 1 patients and 10/26 (38.5%) Cycle 2 patients. The two cohorts differed descriptively in performance status (Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) ≥2:41.7% vs. 87.5%, P<0.001) and malignancy type distribution. RED scores were documented only anecdotally within free-text clinical notes for a subset of Cycle 2 patients and were not systematically recorded or analyzed as a distribution. Conclusions A structured pleural assessment pathway was associated with a statistically significant reduction in emergency presentations and a non-significant reduction in repeated procedures. However, given the small, single-center, non-randomised, uncontrolled before-and-after design, differing case mix between cohorts, and incomplete RED score documentation, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and hypothesis-generating. They support further, larger, multicenter evaluations rather than immediate wider adoption.

papers.abstract_en: The spatial organization of malignant and non-malignant cells within the tumor microenvironment critically influences tumor evolution and therapeutic response. However, the architecture of micro-niches remains incompletely understood. Leveraging Xenium-based spatial transcriptomics, we comprehensively mapped the spatial ecosystem of an orthotopic murine lung cancer model, identifying distinct spatial domains that form unique, organized cellular neighborhoods. These domains cluster into three major communities: (1) non-tumoral regions that recapitulate canonical normal lung structures; (2) a heterogeneous peri-tumoral region composed of spatial domains characterized by mesenchymal remodeling, active immune checkpoint signaling, and immunosuppressive myeloid populations; and (3) intra-tumoral regions that reveal marked tumor nodule heterogeneity, with unique tumor-specific domains exhibiting hallmark cancer pathways. Here, we show that spatial domain analysis resolves tumor nodules into biologically distinct subtypes defined by domain composition, hallmark cancer programs and intercellular communication patterns within the tumor microenvironment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT) is used for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but its effect on postoperative recurrence patterns remains uncertain. We compared overall, locoregional, and distant recurrence after NCIT versus neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT). METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 01 May 2026. Eligible studies included patients with resectable or potentially resectable locally advanced ESCC who received NCIT or NCRT followed by radical esophagectomy. Recurrence outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RRs), and disease-free survival or recurrence-free survival (DFS/RFS) and overall survival (OS) as hazard ratios (HRs), using random-effects models. Post hoc sensitivity analyses excluded studies with marked between-group follow-up imbalance. RESULTS: Twenty comparative studies, all conducted in China, were included; 19 were retrospective observational studies and one was a randomized phase 2 trial. Five studies contributed to the overall-recurrence analysis, and six studies contributed to each of the locoregional- and distant-recurrence analyses. NCIT was associated with lower overall recurrence (RR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.03) and distant recurrence/metastasis (RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.43-0.89; P = 0.009), whereas locoregional recurrence did not differ significantly (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.67-1.55; P = 0.92). In post hoc analyses excluding studies with marked follow-up imbalance, the locoregional estimate remained nonsignificant (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.66-1.15), and the distant-recurrence/metastasis estimate was attenuated and no longer significant (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.36-1.17). Ten studies contributed to OS, which favored NCIT (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48-0.93; P = 0.02; I² = 77%), whereas eight contributed to DFS/RFS, which did not differ significantly (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.59-1.13; P = 0.21; I² = 74%). CONCLUSIONS: Compared with NCRT, NCIT was associated with fewer overall recurrences after radical esophagectomy for locally advanced ESCC. The primary distant-recurrence signal was not robust after excluding studies with marked follow-up imbalance, and no locoregional advantage was demonstrated. These findings do not establish therapeutic superiority and should be interpreted cautiously given the predominance of retrospective evidence, risk of bias, and substantial heterogeneity in survival analyses.

Scratch and Transwell assays were used to detect cell migration and invasion abilities. Western blot was performed to examine the protein expression of prolyl hydroxylase (PHDs) family members, HIF1α, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers E-cadherin and vimentin. The MMF-treated groups received intragastric administration of MMF at a dose of 30 mg/kg daily druing weeks 17-18. The SWY-treated groups were given 20% SWY solution at a dose of 400 mg/kg daily via drinking water druing weeks 17-24, and the remaining groups received plain drinking water. Western blot, immunofluorescence and immunohistochemistry were applied to detect PHDs and HIF1α expression in mouse esophageal tissues, and HE staining was used to verify tumor metastasis. RESULTS: Network toxicology analysis suggestd that fumarate promoted esophageal cancer development by acting on the HIF1α signaling pathway. Fumarate accumulation promoted esophageal cancer cell migration and invasion. The underlying mechanism involved the downregulation of PHD2 and PHD3 by fumarate accumulation (P<0.01), leading to the stabilization and increased expression of HIF1α (P<0.01). This, in turn, facilitated a decrease in E-cadherin protein expression and an increase in vimentin protein expression, thereby promoting esophageal cancer cell metastasis (P<0.05 or P<0.01). papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pneumonia, influenza, asthma, tuberculosis, lung cancer, and COVID-19 are all prevalent in Africa, where they cause a very large burden on the population's health, but are managed by health systems with a limited capacity for prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. They are also underlaid by substantial inequities in outcomes, with the poorest who have no access to care being affected the most. An interdisciplinary group of academics, policymakers, representatives of non-governmental organisations (NGOs), patients, and civil society are implementing a programme to address key respiratory diseases (RD) in five African countries where morbidity and mortality from RD is very large: Nigeria, Kenya, Cameroon, Cote d'Ivoire, and South Africa. The aim is to build capacity, conduct quality research and an intervention trial, and engage communities and policymakers in order to achieve demonstrable and equitable reductions in morbidity and mortality from RD through evidence-based improvements in prevention, diagnosis, treatment, interventions, and policies. The EQUI-RESP-AFRICA project will map the landscape of respiratory medicine in partner countries through rapid reviews of the available literature and data; engage relevant in-country stakeholders; study patients' and providers' preferences and needs; identify research priorities using the Child Health and Nutrition Research Initiative method; and conduct summer schools for capacity building in data science and machine learning/artificial intelligence, in community engagement, and in advocacy for and the use of the Equitable Impact Sensitive Tool (EQUIST) and Pathways to Survival (PATHS) tool. The project will also assess national health system preparedness for emerging infections, identify bottlenecks for early response, assess oxygen capacity and security, study adherence to international guidelines, and conduct qualitative studies to understand barriers to seeking care. It will also explore the feasibility of delivering a pulmonary rehabilitation programme through a randomised controlled trial. Ultimately, the programme will link evidence with policy using the EQUIST and PATHS tools to improve equity in outcomes and identify bottlenecks that lead to morbidity and mortality from respiratory causes. Through high-level meetings, it will prioritise the implementation of equitable interventions that are appropriate to each African context and tailored to patients' needs. A team of social scientists and NGOs, joined by a team of researchers of diverse backgrounds, will engage communities, stakeholders and policymakers to build capacity through summer schools, and disseminate the results through a dedicated project website, the Journal of Global Health, the Journal of the Pan-African Thoracic Society, collaborating NGOs, and mainstream and social media.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Type A thymoma is generally considered a low-risk thymoma subtype with an excellent prognosis and low rates of distant metastasis. Atypical type A thymoma is a recently established entity characterized by more aggressive biological behavior despite retaining the morphology of conventional type A thymoma. Patients with primary conventional type A thymoma who subsequently develop recurrence with atypical histological features are extremely rare. CASE PRESENTATION: A 79-year-old man was referred to our hospital due to gradual enlargement of bilateral pulmonary nodules. Seven years earlier, he had undergone complete resection of an anterior mediastinal tumor, which had been diagnosed as conventional type A thymoma. Retrospective review of preoperative computed tomography images revealed that small pulmonary nodules had already been present at the time of the initial surgery but had yet to be identified. The nodules enlarged slowly from 3 mm to 10 mm and from 3 mm to 7 mm over the 7-year period. Positron emission tomography showed no abnormal fluorodeoxyglucose uptake. After thoracoscopic wedge resection of the left lower lobe lesion, histopathological examination demonstrated pulmonary metastasis of type A thymoma with focal hypercellularity and increased mitotic activity, consistent with atypical type A thymoma. No necrosis was identified. The Ki-67 labeling indices of the primary and metastatic lesions were 7% and 20%, respectively. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that even apparently low-risk type A thymoma may exhibit indolent but metastatic behavior and may develop atypical histological features during a prolonged clinical course. Careful long-term surveillance and detailed pathological evaluation, including assessment of the Ki-67 labeling index, may be important in patients with type A thymoma.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the efficacy of intrapleural anti-PD-1 therapy in elderly patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) complicated by malignant pleural effusion (MPE), and to assess its impact on T-cell subset dynamics. RESULTS: The pleural atresia rates at 5 and 10 weeks were 75.7% and 64.5%, respectively. The objective response rate (ORR) increased from 29.0% at 5 weeks to 38.2% at 10 weeks, and disease control rate (DCR) from 59.9% to 76.4%. Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score improved significantly from baseline (57.3 ± 9.6) to 5 weeks (66.5 ± 9.2) and 10 weeks (74.5 ± 8.3), Borg scores decreased from (6.1 ± 1.3) to (3.8 ± 0.9) and (3.1 ± 0.7), and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) scores decreased from (4.5 ± 1.1) to (2.8 ± 0.5) and (2.2 ± 0.6) (all P<0.01). At 5 weeks, peripheral blood CD3+, CD4+, and CD8+ T cells increased from baseline (53.3 ± 8.6%, 28.25 ± 5.64%, 20.5 ± 4.6%) to (60.5 ± 9.5%, 32.5 ± 7.2%, and 25.2 ± 6.3%), while the CD4+/CD8+ ratio decreased from (1.38 ± 0.11) to (1.29 ± 0.12) (all P<0.01); in pleural effusion, corresponding values rose to (69.5 ± 4.3%, 34.5 ± 6.4%, and 28.8 ± 7.7%), with the ratio falling to (1.19 ± 0.04) (P<0.01). Pleural effusion levels of LDH, TNF-α, and IL-6 all declined from baseline (856.6 ± 130.2 U/L, 48.4 ± 2.3 pg/mL, 74.81 ± 9.17 pg/mL) to 5 weeks (512.5 ± 95.7 U/L, 32.3 ± 3.8 pg/mL, 52.8 ± 7.1 pg/mL) and 10 weeks (385.6 ± 74.8 U/L, 24.9 ± 2.6 pg/mL, 36.6 ± 5.4 pg/mL) (all P<0.01). papers.abstract_en: Predicting disease risk from prior diagnoses is fundamental to clinical decision-making, particularly during health emergencies such as the COVID-19 pandemic, when individuals with long-term conditions may be disproportionately vulnerable to adverse outcomes. Despite intense interest in developing models to predict disease risk from prior diagnoses 1-3 , most prediction models do not estimate effects of each prior diagnosis on disease risk conditional on other diagnoses, limiting interpretability and clinical utility. We developed the Comorbidity Risk Score (CRS), trained on 13 million individuals (age 40-69) from linked electronic health record (EHR) datasets of the entire population of England, to predict COVID-19 hospitalisation and 87 other disease outcomes. CRS was trained at close to saturated sample size and precisely estimated the effects of 212 prior diagnoses on the 88 disease outcomes, conditional on all other prior diagnoses. Correlations of CRS effect sizes across outcomes (e.g. 0.76 for myocardial infarction vs. hyperlipidaemia) matched the corresponding genetic correlations (e.g. 0.79 for myocardial infarction vs. hyperlipidaemia), confirming that comorbidity architectures capture disease aetiology. On average, CRS identified 5% of the population with 3.4-fold higher disease risk, including myocardial infarction (4.4-fold), lung cancer (6.5-fold), and COVID-19 hospitalisation (6.3-fold). Using prior diagnoses alone, CRS outperformed state-of-the-art clinical COVID-19 models 4 . Furthermore, CRS ( N =13 million) substantially outperformed state-of-the-art AI 1 ( N =0.5 million) and linear 3 ( N =0.5 million) models in predicting disease risk, suggesting that training sample size outweighs model complexity. CRS attained near-perfect transferability across self-reported ethnicities (e.g., Black vs. White: AUROC ratio = 97.3%). Finally, CRS distinguished independently predictive comorbidities from indirect associations, e.g., lipid metabolism disorder was a strong predictor of myocardial infarction risk but not ischaemic stroke, after conditioning on other prior diagnoses. In conclusion, CRS provides a comprehensive resource for understanding the impact of comorbidities on COVID-19 and other future diseases, revealing disease aetiology while enabling powerful prediction of disease risk.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening reduces lung cancer mortality but is limited by low uptake and associated with high rates of false-positives and indeterminate-nodules. METHODS: In this pilot study, breath samples were collected from 40 patients with treatment-naïve, pathologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and 25 lung-cancer-screening-eligible healthy controls. Paired samples were analyzed via a compact point-of-care GC-MS platform (CLARION) and a laboratory HRMS reference. Diagnostic classification models were built independently for each platform using elastic net logistic regression with leave-one-out cross-validation, and performance was evaluated by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RESULTS: CLARION identified 103 VOCs across breath specimens, compared to over 900 identified by HRMS. Despite this difference in panel size, CLARION achieved diagnostic performance nearly identical to HRMS for distinguishing NSCLC cases from controls (AUC 0.864 vs. 0.863). Compared to controls, performance statistics were similar for early-stage NSCLC (AUC 0.854 vs. 0.841) and adenocarcinoma (AUC 0.770 vs. 0.787). VOCs of interest include p-cymene, phenol, propylbenzene, tetradecane, β-ocimene, 2,3-dihydro-indole, and 1-methylthio-(Z)-1-propene. CONCLUSION: A compact, point-of-care breath GC-MS platform achieved diagnostic performance for NSCLC detection comparable to a laboratory HRMS reference despite a substantially smaller detected VOC panel. These findings support continued development of point-of-care breath VOC testing as a non-invasive, field-deployable complement to LDCT-based lung cancer screening.

papers.abstract_en: People with lung cancer commonly experience stigma, however, the temporal impacts are poorly understood. This study investigated changes (using linear mixed modelling) and trajectories (using latent growth modelling) of stigma over a 6-month period in people newly diagnosed with lung cancer, who were participants of a larger trial of supportive care interventions (ACTRN12615000932561). Relatively higher stigma trajectories were associated with younger age and a history of smoking. papers.abstract_en: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based technologies have the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy while reducing tissue loss in small biopsies. In non-small-cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC), small biopsies often limit ancillary testing. We aimed to develop a deep learning-based framework for automated histopathological classification of NSCLC subtypes. Archived hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images from 341 NSCLC and benign specimens were digitized and annotated by two expert pathologists. A two-stage Dense Net121-based cascade was employed: Stage 1 differentiated not otherwise specified (NOS) from not-NOS specimens; Stage 2 classified not-NOS into adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, or non-cancerous tissue. Patient-level predictions were derived via majority voting. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. In Stage 1, NOS versus not-NOS classification achieved 0.92 patient-level accuracy. In Stage 2, accuracy for adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and non-cancer was 0.94, with perfect classification of non-cancer patients (precision, recall, and F1 = 1.00). In the final step, the combined analysis demonstrated an overall accuracy of 0.88, with recall rates of 1.00 for adenocarcinoma and non-cancer, 0.83 for squamous cell carcinoma, and 0.67 for NOS. The proposed two-stage model demonstrated strong performance across NSCLC subtypes, including the diagnostically challenging NOS group. This approach may reduce reliance on ancillary tests, accelerate diagnosis, and optimize tissue preservation.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is a dynamically evolving disease characterized by marked temporal heterogeneity across tumor progression, treatment response, resistance development, and clinical outcomes. Nevertheless, the majority of existing artificial intelligence (AI) systems continue to rely predominantly on single time-point imaging, imposing inherent constraints on their capacity to characterize disease evolution and capture continuously shifting risk states. The growing availability of longitudinal imaging data, combined with ongoing advances in temporal deep learning, is driving a transition in lung cancer AI from static image interpretation toward dynamic risk prediction. In this narrative review, relevant literature was identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus from database inception to September 2026, using terms related to lung cancer, longitudinal imaging, temporal deep learning, and dynamic risk prediction, with representative studies selected according to their methodological relevance, clinical applications, and implications for clinical translation. Longitudinal imaging tracks disease trajectories over time and offers distinct opportunities to characterize tumor growth dynamics, treatment-induced changes, and evolving recurrence risk. Temporal deep learning, in turn, enables the modelling of complex time-dependent relationships that conventional static approaches are poorly suited to represent. The field has progressed from early dual time-point analyses to long-range temporal modelling, multimodal temporal fusion, and continuous risk updating, with encouraging applications spanning pulmonary nodule management, treatment response assessment, recurrence surveillance, survival prediction, and individualized disease management. Nonetheless, substantial obstacles persist, including the scarcity of large-scale longitudinal datasets, irregular temporal sampling, limited model generalizability, insufficient causal interpretability, and a lack of robust evidence supporting real-world clinical deployment. Addressing these challenges will require coordinated efforts toward standardized longitudinal data infrastructure, continuous-time modelling frameworks, multimodal integration strategies, and closer alignment of AI systems with clinical workflows. Taken together, longitudinal imaging and temporal deep learning are steering lung cancer AI away from static image analysis and toward dynamic disease management, with the potential to support continuous risk assessment and potentially inform adaptive clinical decision-making throughout the full spectrum of lung cancer care.

papers.abstract_en: Epigenetic age, influenced by environmental factors like smoking, predicts mortality in general populations but remains under-explored in early-stage lung cancer. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved dramatically over the past decade with the advent of widespread genetic testing, immunotherapy, and targeted therapies. Treatments directed against epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and other driver mutations have reduced toxicity and improved efficacy for selected patients. Ultimately, given the lack of durable response and his inability to tolerate chemotherapy, the patient opted for palliative care. DISCUSSION: Patients with actionable targets such as EGFR, BRCA1/2, or elevated PD-L1 generally have superior outcomes with targeted and combination therapy compared with patients who lack targetable options. However, coexisting mutations can interact and provide escape mechanisms. papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Oncogenic KRAS mutations drive 25-30% of western lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) cases, however the mechanisms that restrain tumor progression remain poorly defined. N-Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein (N-WASP) regulates actin cytoskeleton dynamics and epithelial architecture, but its role in KRAS-driven lung tumorigenesis is unclear. METHODS: We generated a conditional N-WASP knockout in KRASG12D-driven lung adenocarcinoma mice (N-WASPLKO/KRASG12D) using Sftpc-CreERT2, and assessed N-WASP knockdown A549 cells (A549KD) in 3D culture for tumor burden, ERK signaling, transcriptomic changes, and E-cadherin expression. The tumors isolated from these mice retained strong pro-surfactant protein C expression, confirming alveolar epithelial origin and predominantly adopted a solid growth pattern, indicative of disrupted epithelial organization. Mechanistically, N-WASP loss enhanced KRAS-driven ERK1/2 activation in lung tissue, consistent with increased mitogenic signaling. In A549 cells, N-WASP deficiency disrupted cytoskeletal architecture, promoted proliferation, and impaired cell-cell adhesion, recapitulating in vivo tumor phenotypes. A kinase inhibitor screen identified Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) activity as a driver of this hyperproliferative phenotype, with ROCK inhibition normalizing proliferation in N-WASP-deficient cells, linking elevated Rho/ROCK signaling to the increased ERK1/2 activation observed upon N-WASP loss. CONCLUSION: These results establish N-WASP as a critical suppressor of KRAS-driven lung adenocarcinoma, linking cytoskeletal integrity to oncogenic signaling and transcriptional regulation. Our findings highlight the interplay between actin dynamics, epithelial architecture, and KRAS signaling, suggesting that targeting N-WASP dependent pathways could modulate lung cancer aggressiveness and offer novel therapeutic opportunities.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Cisplatin has been a standard chemotherapeutic agent for advanced non-small cell lung cancer for decades. Conventionally administered intravenously, it undergoes systemic distribution, exposing both tumour and healthy tissues to the drug. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle injection of cisplatin is emerging as a potential intratumoural drug delivery (ITDD) strategy. However, rigorous preclinical research is needed before ITDD can be more widely adopted. METHODS: We used our experimentally induced ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma (OPA) model, generated by Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus (JSRV) infection, to evaluate transthoracic and transbronchial ITDD techniques. We compared systemic platinum exposure following intravenous cisplatin delivery with that following intratumoural cisplatin administration. Both non-recovery and recovery studies were conducted in a total of eight sheep. RESULTS: ITDD techniques were successfully developed and performed in three tumour bearing sheep during non-recovery procedures. To provide a reference for systemic platinum exposure, intravenous cisplatin was administered to three JSRV-infected sheep that did not develop OPA. Intravenous administration produced a rapid plasma platinum peak followed by a rapid decline. ITDD resulted in preferential platinum deposition within targeted lung tumours while producing substantially lower systemic platinum exposure compared with intravenous administration. Intratumoural cisplatin delivery was also evaluated in a recovery procedure using a single sheep, comparing single-site and fractionated administration over a 28-day period, with tumour biopsies confirming lesion presence before treatment. Following ITDD, tumour volumes were observed to decrease over the study period. The recovery experiments demonstrated the feasibility of repeated tumour biopsies, intratumoural injections, longitudinal CT monitoring and recovery anaesthesia using the OPA model. DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first report of direct intratumoural cisplatin administration into ovine lung tumours. This study also provides proof-of-concept that this clinically relevant large animal lung cancer model can serve as a translational platform for evaluating intratumoural therapeutic delivery strategies relevant to human lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Mediastinal epidermoid cysts are exceptionally rare benign lesions, particularly in the anterior mediastinum. Their nonspecific clinical and radiological features may resemble other anterior mediastinal masses, including thymic lesions and mature cystic teratomas, making preoperative diagnosis challenging. CASE PRESENTATION: A 35-year-old man with no relevant medical or surgical history presented with a 2-month history of retrosternal chest pain. Clinical examination and cardiac evaluation were unremarkable. Chest radiography demonstrated mediastinal widening, while contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed a well-defined anterior mediastinal mass measuring approximately 7 × 5 × 3 cm. CT-guided biopsy and fluid aspiration initially suggested a mature cystic teratoma without immature or malignant elements. The patient underwent complete excision using a three-port video-assisted thoracoscopic approach. Intraoperatively, the cyst was densely adherent to the pericardium and contained thick purulent material. Hair-like material and firm cartilage-like areas were observed grossly but were not confirmed histologically. Culture of the cyst contents yielded Staphylococcus aureus. Histopathological examination demonstrated a squamous epithelial lining with chronic inflammation, granulation tissue, and fibrosis, confirming an infected mediastinal epidermoid cyst. The discrepancy between the initial cytological impression and the final histopathological diagnosis highlights the limitations of imaging and needle biopsy in evaluating rare cystic mediastinal lesions. CONCLUSION: Complete surgical excision provides both definitive diagnosis and effective treatment. Epidermoid cysts should be considered in the differential diagnosis of cystic anterior mediastinal masses. Video-assisted thoracoscopic excision may be feasible in carefully selected patients, even in the presence of dense pericardial adhesions.

papers.abstract_en: Thymic cysts are uncommon benign lesions of the anterior mediastinum and are frequently detected incidentally on imaging studies. Microscopic thymoma and microthymoma are extremely rare microscopic thymic epithelial proliferations that are usually identified only by histopathological examination. Their relationship to thymic cysts and to each other remains poorly understood. A 54-year-old woman was referred to our institution after an anterior mediastinal lesion was incidentally detected on routine chest computed tomography (CT). Magnetic resonance imaging and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT findings were consistent with a thymic cyst. Robot-assisted thoracoscopic resection of the cyst with the adjacent thymic tissue was performed for definitive diagnosis and treatment. Histopathological examination revealed a unilocular thymic cyst accompanied by two incidental microscopic thymic epithelial lesions within the adjacent thymic tissue: a 0.6-mm microscopic thymoma and a 2.0-mm Type A microthymoma. Based on their characteristic size and histological features, both lesions were diagnosed without additional immunohistochemical analysis. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remains free of recurrence 18 months after surgery. To our knowledge, the coexistence of microscopic thymoma and Type A microthymoma adjacent to a thymic cyst is exceptionally rare. The close proximity and similar histological features of these lesions suggest that they may represent different stages within a continuous morphological spectrum of microscopic thymic epithelial proliferations rather than entirely distinct entities. Furthermore, this case highlights the potential value of careful pathological examination of thymic tissue adjacent to resected thymic cysts for detecting occult microscopic epithelial lesions and improving pathological assessment.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumor (SMARCA4-UT) is a recently recognized, rare, and highly aggressive malignancy. No standard treatment has been established for unresectable disease, and the prognosis is generally poor. These tumors often grow rapidly, and bulky masses can cause clinically significant symptoms. CASE PRESENTATION: A 52-year-old man with a history of heavy smoking presented with chest and back pain. Imaging revealed a large mediastinal mass. A CT-guided biopsy demonstrated an undifferentiated neoplasm with complete loss of BRG1 (SMARCA4) expression, a high proliferative index (Ki-67 labeling index, 80%), and no evidence of specific lineage differentiation, findings consistent with SMARCA4-UT. Subsequent comprehensive genomic profiling revealed a SMARCA4 nonsense mutation and a high tumor mutational burden. The tumor was clinically unresectable and showed rapid progression, resulting in severe dyspnea and syncope due to marked extrinsic airway compression. Because a high-grade sarcoma was initially suspected before the final diagnosis of SMARCA4-UT was established, first-line doxorubicin plus ifosfamide (AI) therapy was administered, resulting in rapid symptomatic relief and a partial response. However, after three cycles of AI therapy, the disease progressed clinically with a left adrenal metastasis. Subsequent treatment with the immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) atezolizumab plus carboplatin and paclitaxel showed no objective response, and the patient died 6 months after the initiation of systemic therapy. CONCLUSION: This case suggests that doxorubicin plus ifosfamide may provide rapid but transient tumor shrinkage and symptomatic improvement in thoracic SMARCA4-UT with airway obstruction. This regimen may be considered when urgent tumor reduction is required to relieve impending airway compromise. However, early diagnosis may also be important because first-line ICI-containing regimens have been associated with improved clinical outcomes in thoracic SMARCA4-UT.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a highly aggressive malignant tumor which suffers from poor prognosis and limited therapeutic remedies. As a physiologically-oriented radiotherapy and highly tumor-specific modality, boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) shows great potential for the treatment of ESCC. Since efficacy of BNCT is critically restricted to boron drugs, novel boron agents with satisfactory boron load and intracellular uptake are highly demanded. Herein, we developed a novel albumin/BSH-conjugated nanoparticle (BSH@Alb) as a safe and effective boron agent. It resulted BSH@Alb displayed uniform particle size, high encapsulation efficiency (93.1 ± 0.39%), loading capacity (15.52 ± 0.41%) and good stability in different solution (water, PBS and plasma). Collectively, BSH@Alb significantly enhanced intracellular boron accumulation and showed acceptable cytocompatibility in comparison with prototype BSH, supporting its potential value for BNCT therapy as a promising boron-delivery candidate.

papers.abstract_en: Breast cancer and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) are most prevalent forms of malignancies worldwide and are associated with BRCA2 variants. While BRCA2 pathogenic variants are well established in breast cancer, their transcriptional consequences in lung adenocarcinoma remain poorly characterized, and no study has directly compared the shared differentially expressed gene (DEG) signature between BRCA2-variant metastatic breast cancer and BRCA2-variant LUAD. In this study, we used an integrative bioinformatics approach to identify and characterize this shared transcriptomic profile using publicly available TCGA and GEO datasets accessed via cBioPortal. Top dysregulated genes were subjected to protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis using STRING and Cytoscape (CytoHubba, MCC algorithm), functional enrichment through Metascape and survival analysis through UALCAN, with disease associations validated against the DISEASES database. SERPINA1, PIGR, FGG and FCGBP were identified as candidate hub genes, common in both types of malignancies. The breast cancer gene set was associated with impaired BRCA2-RAD51-mediated homologous recombination, and the lung dataset had strong signatures of alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells and signatures specific to lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). SERPINA1 and PIGR were significant markers in breast cancer and FGG was significant marker in LUAD. The findings identify a partially overlapping epithelial transcriptional profile associated with BRCA2-variant breast and lung tumor datasets. However, these observations represent associations within BRCA2-altered cohorts and do not establish that BRCA2 dysfunction directly drives the identified transcriptional changes. SERPINA1, PIGR, FGG, and FCGBP therefore represent candidate tissue-dependent biomarkers requiring independent validation.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Choroidal metastases may cause substantial visual impairment in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although local ocular treatments are frequently considered, targeted systemic therapy may provide effective control in tumors harboring actionable mutations. We report the rapid regression of a choroidal metastasis following first-line osimertinib therapy in a patient with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated NSCLC. CASE PRESENTATION: A 59-year-old man with metastatic EGFR-mutated NSCLC presented with progressive visual decline in the left eye. Ophthalmic examination revealed a peripapillary choroidal lesion associated with serous retinal detachment. Optical coherence tomography demonstrated subretinal fluid, consistent with a choroidal metastasis. First-line osimertinib therapy had been initiated 12 days before presentation at our clinic. An early reduction in subretinal fluid was observed during follow-up, followed by complete resolution at the 2-month follow-up. This was accompanied by regression of the choroidal lesion and improvement in visual function. No local ocular treatment was required. CONCLUSION: First-line osimertinib may induce rapid regression of choroidal metastases in patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC. In selected cases, an early response to systemic targeted therapy may allow local ocular treatment to be avoided.

papers.abstract_en: The individual incidences of lung cancer and cardiovascular disease in the elderly population mean that there is a strong likelihood of both occurring simultaneously. Common practice for severe aortic stenosis (AS) would be surgical aortic valve replacement (AVR), unless deemed high-risk for this surgical procedure. Age and lung cancer both increase a patient's surgical risk; hence, the less invasive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) to manage valve disease ahead of lung resection for lung cancer is an acceptable alternative after assessing other factors such as procedural risk, comorbidities, and prognosis. We present the case of an 82-year-old female patient who underwent a TAVI seven months before lung resection for an incidental diagnosis of lung cancer with staging T1b N0 M0. Postoperatively, she was treated for atrial fibrillation and lung collapse, then discharged after resolution of these complications on the eighth day after surgery, and remained well at follow-up three months later. This case report explores a situation when this sequence of interventions was appropriate due to increased surgical risk in the elderly population.

papers.abstract_en: Cardiac tamponade is a life-threatening emergency classically associated with Beck's triad of hypotension, muffled heart sounds, and elevated jugular venous pressure; however, incomplete or atypical presentations may delay diagnosis. We report the case of a previously healthy 28-year-old woman who presented with progressive dyspnoea, pleuritic chest pain, orthopnoea, peripheral oedema, fever, and fatigue. Examination revealed mild tachycardia, soft heart sounds, reduced basal air entry, and ankle oedema, while the patient remained normotensive. Initial investigations demonstrated cardiomegaly with pleural effusions on chest radiograph, low-voltage QRS complexes on electrocardiogram, and markedly raised inflammatory markers. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography identified a large anterior mediastinal mass encasing the great vessels, a significant pericardial effusion with features of cardiac tamponade, and bilateral pleural effusions. Emergency pericardiocentesis resulted in immediate clinical improvement. Histopathological analysis confirmed high-grade B-cell lymphoma, most consistent with primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma. The patient was treated with immunochemotherapy, achieving complete metabolic remission on end-of-treatment PET-CT. This case highlights the importance of recognising atypical presentations of cardiac tamponade and considering mediastinal malignancy in young patients presenting with unexplained cardiorespiratory symptoms.
